Senator Tepler, Representative Doudera, and members of the Committee, I am Laura
Paye, the Hydropower Coordinator for the Bureau of Land Resources in the Maine Department of Environmental Protection, speaking neither for nor against L.D. 1698.
This bill proposes to amend Maine's Release from Dam Ownership and Water Level
Maintenance laws, located in Title 38 Sections 901-908. These statutes outline a
process for an owner of a non-hydropower dam to petition the Maine Department of
Environmental Protection for release from ownership or water level maintenance. The Department currently has before it the first instance of petitions that have been
accepted for processing under Title 38 Sections 901-908.

The Department proposed a bill earlier this session, L.D. 62, which would amend these sections of statute. The Committee amended L.D. 62 to incorporate provisions from
other related bills and other Department suggestions before voting the bill ought to pass
as amended. If the Committee desires, the Department believes that many of the provisions of L.D. 1698 could also be combined with L.D. 62. The Department has
been working with Representative Milliken, municipal officials, the Department of Inland
Fisheries and Wildlife (lF\/\/) and the Maine Emergency Management Agency (MEMA)
to determine which elements of L.D. 1698 should be combined with the provisions of
L.D. 62. The Department suggests that many of the provisions of Section 1 of L.D. 1698 should be retained, with some edits. After consulting with IFW and MEMA, the Department does not recommend keeping sections 2 through 4 of the bill. However, we do recommend additional changes based on consultation with IFW and MEMA.
Attached to this testimony, the Department has provided proposed further amendments to L.D. 62 that would incorporate many of the provisions of L.D. 1698, as well as
additional changes suggested by IFW and MEMA that the Department agrees are
important. The proposed L.D. 62 amendment is color-coded to show the Department's
recommended changes based on the provisions of L.D. 1698 and IFW and MEMA
recommendations, as well as the previously incorporated provisions of L.D. 430. if the Committee wishes, it could reconsider L.D. 62 and combine the provisions of that bill
with L.D. 1698. Either bill could ultimately serve as the vehicle to move the attached amendment forward.
Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony on this bill. I would be happy to answer any questions from the Committee.

Testimony ofRepresentative Nina Milliken presenting
LD 1698, An Act Regarding Changes of Ownership of Dams
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Environment and Natural Resources

Good morning, Senator Tepler, Representative Gramlich, and friends and colleagues on the Joint
Standing Committee on Environment and Natural Resources. My name is Nina Milliken and I
happily represent the folks of Blue Hill, Brooksville, Castine, Sedgwick, Surry and Trenton in
the Maine House. Today I am here to present LD 1698, An Act Regarding Changes of
Ownership of Dams.
Recently, I came before this committee to present a bill to amend the dam abandonment law that was passed in the mid-90s. As I stated then, Hancock County is currently facing a difficult
situation where three dams are in the process of being abandoned. In the 1990s, the Legislature
laid out a process for dam abandonment. The process has never been done to completion and
because of that, many of the challenges in the statute had not been discovered until my
communities and those of Representative Bishop were thrust into this process last year. This
committee voted unanimously on LD 62, which will amend that statute.
A short time later, this bill, LD 1698, was printed. This bill seeks to add even more changes to
the same statute. I notified your analyst and chairs and asked that they hold onto LD 62 so this
committee could decide how best to proceed with the two bills. I also reached out to Laura Paye
at the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and she crafted this amendment, which I believe does a great job stitching together the two separate bills into one. I trust this committee to
do whatever they see as the best Way forward, but as the sponsor of both bills, I support a merging of the two with this amendment----if that is also how the committee thinks it is best to
proceed.
I'll take a minute to briefly remind the committee of the reason for these bills. BuckMill is a salvage company that currently owns three dams in Hancock County and is trying to abandon them based on the statute passed in the mid-90s. They have not been a good faith negotiator with
District 16: Blue Hill, Brooksville, Castine, Sedgwick, Surry and Trenton

the communities impacted by this process. They have consistently done the bare minimum required in that statute, which has presented enormous challenges to the five impacted
communities in deciding how to proceed. We have jumped through many hoops and done an
enormous amount of work to sort it all out, but we are keenly aware of the absolute need to add
more teeth to the statute to make sure that other communities in the future do not need to go through such chaos and fear when they are faced with this same issue------there are an enormous
amount of aging dams in every corner of our state. LD 1698 adds to the teeth that were added by LD 62.
I appreciate all of your time and consideration and am happy to try to answer any questions.
